doc.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Delivering newspapers past the Sunset Cafe and watching Louis Armstrong
summary: Hinton remembers hanging around Armstrong's rehearsals and looking into the Sunset Cafe at 5:30 am as a paperboy, deciding that was where he had to be.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well just tell me something. Did you get a chance to get any, just a taste of Louis Armstrong playing with Lil Armstrong and the boys that came, the fellas that came from New Orleans?

Well I was with the fellas when they were in rehearsal, and I came out when he had the Hot Five with the Kid Ory, with the Kid Ory in there. And I started coming to rehearsals and standing right there, he says, “Son get back you’re standing in the way,” you know? But that was my impression, that was my introduction to show business. I’m listening, about 5:30 in the morning I’m delivering my newspapers down by that Sunset Cafe, and I’d look in the window at 5:30 in the morning and I’ve got my paper sack on my back, and there’s all them guys, Louis and all of them in tuxedos there, and a nice cold glass in his hand, and a nice lady standing there. And I’ve got my paper sack on my back and I look and I say, that’s where I got to be. That’s why we’re here now.
Yeah, they always had their lady there, and the waiters is putting the chairs up on the table, and it’s all over, the night is all over, it’s 5:30 in the morning.
Well I’ve often said that I had that choice between tuxedo and overalls, that was the choice when we grew up.
